City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
May 7, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:01 p.m. , on May 7, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on May 02, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
INVOCATION: Council Member Leckness
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Labor Negotiations - ?The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are the City and the City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council gave direction to staff regarding labor negotiations but there was no reportable action from Closed Session.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Proclaim May 6-12, 2012, as â??Wildfire Awareness Week"
Mayor Ury presented the proclamation to OCFA Battalion Chief Mike Ferdig.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Gail Reavis, M.V.: outlined her attendance at Arts Alive over the weekend and her walk along the beautiful Oso Creek Trail.
Larry Gilbert, M.V.: provided an update on state issues and stated that there are two pending bills on tax increment financing and regardless of what the legislature does, he is sure the Governor will veto the bills.
Wil Garcia, M.V.: thanked the City Council for initiating the tennis center renovation project and he encouraged the Council Members to vote in favor of the landscape and irrigation item on the agenda tonight.
Lamar Kelsoe, M.V.: suggested that the Council would better serve the working community if the meetings started at 7:00 p.m.
Helen Workun, M.V.: announced that she couldn’t have been more proud of Mission Viejo at the Arts Alive festival and she thanked City staff for their ability to put the event together.
Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: stated that the City’s partnership with the Nadadores for a shuttle service during the recent swim meet was great. She thanked Mayor Ury for making presentations at the event and she also commented on the phenomenal day at the lake for Mission Viejo’s adopted Marines. Ms. Bucknum noted that Arts Alive and the National Day of Prayer service were huge successes for the community.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Item 8 was not removed from the Consent Calendar, however the Council allowed time for Public Works Director Mark Chagnon to address a question on the item.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
2.
City Council Minutes
Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of April, 16, 2012, as presented.
3.

Ratified the accompanying check register.
4.

5.

6.
Claim Against the City - Rubin vs. City of Mission Viejo
Rejected the claim.
7.
2012 Fourth of July Community Street Faire
Approved the Special Events Permit submitted by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee authorizing the annual Mission Viejo Fourth of July Community Street Faire on Wednesday, July 4, 2012.
8.
2012 Residential Resurfacing-Asphalt Overlay (CIP 838)
Public Works Director Mark Chagnon outlined the boundaries of the area scheduled to be resurfaced.
Approved the bid specifications and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.
PUBLIC HEARINGS
9.
Reconsideration of Amendment to Conditions of Approval for Planned Development Permit PDP2010-232 and Minor Exception ME2011-99 submitted by UDR Pacific Los Alisos LP for the construction of a three-level multifamily complex on 10.83 acres at 28601 Los Alisos Boulevard in the RPD 30 (Residential Planned Development) zone. The reconsideration request pertains to possible modification to the terms of affordability of the project’s 48 affordable housing units in lieu of removing the requirement for affordability from the conditions of approval
Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report. At the hour of 6:28 p.m., Mayor Ury opened the public hearing. Don MacKenzie, Managing Director of UDR Development: outlined UDR’s new proposal.
The following spoke in support of the proposal: Gail Reavis, M.V.; Larry Gilbert, M.V.; and Susan Sellers, M.V.
The following spoke in opposition to the new UDR proposal: Christian Abasto, Public Law Center, Santa Ana; Donald Landis, M.V.; and Cesar Covarrubias, Executive Director of The Kennedy Commission, Irvine.
Don MacKenzie, Managing Director of UDR Development: responded to comments made during the public testimony.
At the hour of 6:45 p.m., Mayor Ury closed the public hearing.
The City Council Members made comments and asked questions of Mr. MacKenzie.
John Ramirez, Legal Counsel for UDR: responded to the City Council Members questions.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to adopt Resolution 12-23 , as amended, Approving a Request Submitted by UDR Pacific Los Alisos LP, to Modify the Applicable Conditions of Approval in Previously Approved City Council Resolution No. 11-54 Approving Planned Development Permit PDP2010-232 and Minor Exception ME2011-99 for the Construction of a Three-level Multifamily Complex on 10.83 Acres at 28601 Los Alisos Boulevard in the RPD 30 (Residential Planned Development) Zone, to Require That 24 Units be Reserved as Affordable Housing Units Instead of 48 Units as Previously Approved.
The Resolution will be amended to direct that the applicant provide $400,000 of the total $3,636,000 in park fees once (1) the plan check approval has been completed, (2) the affordable housing agreement pertaining to the 24 affordable units has been fully negotiated and approved by both the City and UDR, and (3) the thirty day Public Resources Code statute of limitations has lapsed. UDR will pay the remainder of the park fees when the building permit is pulled.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht
ABSENT:
None
OLD BUSINESS
The Old Business items were taken out of order.
12.
Mission Viejo Library Story Time Room Remodel (CIP 601)
Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.
The following expressed support for the Story Time Room remodel: Jennifer Hambel, President of the Mission Viejo Chapter MOMS Club, M.V, and Kim, Sammi and Zoe Corwin, M.V.
The following expressed opposition to the amount of money proposed for the room remodel: Lamar Kelsoe, M.V.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to award the contract for the subject project to Optima RPM, Inc. in the amount $358,344.00.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht
ABSENT:
None
11.
Approve the Deeds and Easement Between the City of Mission Viejo and the County of Orange for a Land Swap for Recreational and Park Purposes
Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.
The following presented written comments in favor of the land swap and a dog park: Cari Cohn-Morros, M.V. and Barry Inciong, M.V.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to authorize the City Manager, subject to any minor revisions required by the City Attorney or City Engineer to: (1) sign the Quit Claim Deed for the land swap of 2.71 acres of County park land to the City of Mission Viejo; and (2) sign the Quit Claim Deed for the land swap of 7.18 acres of City land to the County of Orange for the Arroyo Trabuco trail connection.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
ABSENT:
None
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to sign the Easement Deed for 1.54 acres of City land for County trail access.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None

None
10.
Marguerite Tennis Center Renovation Project (CIP 501)
This item was not considered (see action for item 22.)
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
Mayor Ury
22.
Marguerite Tennis Center Renovation Project (CIP501)
Mayor Ury presented his report.
Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) approve a Change Order to the construction contract with Western Alta Construction Company for installation of the irrigation system for the project in the amount of $357,585; and (2) adopt Resolution 12-26 Amending the Fiscal Year 2011-2012 Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement Marguerite Tennis Center Project 501 by utilizing the $400,000 commitment from UDR for park fees (made earlier in the meeting.)
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury

Council Member Schlicht
ABSENT:
None

City Attorney's Report
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)
21.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at the Orange County Sheriff’s Medal of Valor luncheon which honors law enforcement personnel who have gone above and beyond. She was pleased to see a former Mission Viejo deputy and school resource officer, Quyen Vuong, receive the Medal of Merit for his innovative “Text-a-Tip” program. She further acknowledged two deputies who are Mission Viejo residents: Eric Brown received the Lifesaving Medal and Marcus Perez received the Medal of Valor. Council Member Kelley stated that it is very comforting to know that the Orange County Sheriff’s Department is protecting the community. She also commended staff for their fine work on the Earth Day event and the Marine lake day. She further thanked Marine Adoption Committee Chairman Bruce Hunt for all of his hard work to bring a “day of paradise” to the Marines. Council Member Kelley discussed her attendance at additional events including the Children’s Environmental Fair, the Mayor’s Prayer Breakfast, the National Day of Prayer ceremony at the civic center, and Arts Alive festival. Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the month of May is moral courage.
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Leckness thanked Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay for displaying the Arts Alive Festival banners to advertise the dates of the event. The banners provided a constant reminder and there was a great turnout both days.
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht announced that today is the 10th anniversary of the opening of city hall. She outlined her attendance at four National Day of Prayer events and she noted that the main theme was that we are a nation in crisis. She stated that these are tough economic times and she doesn’t think the Council is making the right choices with the City’s finances. Council Member Schlicht asked her colleagues to pay attention to the reports and look at the cumulative effect of the spending. She concluded her comments with a quote from Thomas Sowell, "No matter how disastrously some policy has turned out, anyone who criticizes it can expect to hear: ‘But what would you replace it with?'"
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon echoed Council Member Kelley’s comments on the Medal of Valor luncheon. She stated that it was inspiring and it gave her pause to be grateful for our own police force and those who protect the City. She too attended several National Day of Prayer events and she noted that the ceremony at Mission Viejo’s civic center was extremely special to her and she hopes the city will continue to support it. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon outlined her attendance at various events including a Model United Nations competition, an Eagle Scout ceremony, Vocational Visions “An Enchanted Evening with Country Flair,” a League of Cities meeting in Dana Point, an Earth Day event at Newhart Middle School, an Elks Club scholarship presentation and the Arts Alive festival. Council Member Reardon also announced that the Mission Viejo Drumline Boosters Club is seeking donations and it is a worthy cause for a group of very talented musicians.
Mayor Ury
Mayor Ury thanked Keith Rattay for a wonderful job on Arts Alive and he announced that he had a great time handing out awards at the recent Nadadores event. He discussed perception and leadership and stated that the City benefits from having five Council Members instead of just one. He noted that the Council is charged with making financial decisions that will be advantageous to the residents and his time on the Council has very little to do with governing out of fear. He is interested in the art of what’s possible and the art of what the Council can do to benefit the citizens of Mission Viejo. Mayor Ury reminded his colleagues that he challenged them to spend more time on economic development and to evaluate the choices that they make. He also announced that the City of Anaheim has implemented a Business Concierge program with student volunteers who guide new business owners as they come to town. Mayor Ury announced that he plans to sit down with staff to come up with ideas for a similar program to help business in Mission Viejo grow and flourish. Finally, he noted that the State of California is not going to fix itself from the top down but rather from the bottom up. The Council needs to make investments in areas that benefit a large part of the population and an investment in Mission Viejo businesses.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 9:55 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, May 21, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
